newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey releases jailed Kurdish newspaper editor.
newsitem.headline: Turkey releases jailed Kurdish newspaper editor.

text.p: Turkish authorities released newspaper editor Isik Yurtcu on Friday, one day after parliament passed a partial amnesty for imprisoned journalists, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
Under the new law, newspaper editors regarded as legally responsible for the content of their papers will have their trials halted or their sentences suspended for three years.
Yurtcu was jailed in 1994 for a series of articles about the Kurdish guerrilla campaign in southeast Turkey published in the pro-Kurdish daily Ozgur Gundem.
Yurtcu was the paper's "responsible editor", which means he both managed the reporting staff and was legally responsible for articles printed.
The U.S.-based Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) visited Turkey last month to present Yurtcu with an award for his fight for freedom of the press.
The visit sparked government calls for a change in the law to allow the release of imprisoned journalists.
The CPJ said in July there were 78 journalists in Turkey's prisons, the highest number of any country in the world.
Rights activists say the new law does not prevent continued prosecution of journalists who produce stories in violation of Turkey's many limits on press freedom.
